chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hanan ibn Sadeer, from Yazeed ibn Khalifa, and he is a man from the Banu al-Harith ibn Ka'b, who said:

I heard him saying, 'I went to Medina, and Ziyad ibn Ubayd Allah al-Harithi was its governor. So I sought permission to enter upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), entered, greeted him, and settled in my place. I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'I am a man from Banu al-Harith ibn Ka'b, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has guided me to your love and affection, O People of the Household.' He said to me, 'And how have you been guided to our affection, O People of the Household? By Allah, our love in Banu al-Harith ibn Ka'b is scarce.'

He said, 'I said to him, 'May I be your ransom! I have a Khurasani slave who works as a bleacher, and he has four fellow countrymen. They invite each other every Friday, and the invitation falls upon one of them, so my slave's turn comes every five Fridays. He prepares Nabidh and meat for them. He said that when they finish eating the food and meat, he brings a bowl, fills it with Nabidh, then brings a clean jug. When he hands it to one of them, he says to him, 'Do not drink until you send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad.' Thus I was guided to your love through this slave.'

He said, 'So he said to me, 'Advise him well, and convey greetings from me to him, and say to him that Ja'far ibn Muhammad says to you: 'Look at this drink of yours which you are drinking. If a lot of it intoxicates, do not approach the little of it, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Every intoxicant is forbidden,' and said: 'Whatever a lot of it intoxicates, the little of it is forbidden.'

He said, 'So I went to Kufa and conveyed the greetings to the slave from Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him). He wept, then said to me, 'Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) took such care of me that he conveyed greetings to me?' I said, 'Yes, and he told me to say to you: 'Look at this drink of yours which you are drinking. If a lot of it intoxicates, do not approach the little of it, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Every intoxicant is forbidden, and whatever a lot of it intoxicates, the little of it is forbidden,' and he advised me regarding you. Therefore go, for you are free for the sake of Allah, the Exalted.' The slave said, 'By Allah, it is a drink that will not enter my stomach as long as I remain in the world.'

key_terms.إِجَّانَة: Ijjana (a type of bowl or vessel)
key_terms.النَّبِيذ: Nabidh (fermented drink, usually from dates or raisins)
key_terms.لِوَجْهِ اللَّهِ: Li-wajhi Allah (for the sake of Allah)

ai.seo_question: How did a slave's habit of serving Nabidh lead his master to the love of the Ahl al-Bayt?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the practical application of the principle of *kathir wa qalil* (abundance and scarcity) in determining the prohibition of wine, a key juristic distinction in Shia fiqh. The narrative highlights the social role of the Ahl al-Bayt in guiding even non-Arab servants, culminating in the slave’s voluntary manumotion as a sign of gratitude and spiritual elevation. It underscores the link between doctrinal adherence to the Prophet’s teachings and personal piety, where the slave’s vow to abstain reflects the transformative power of the Imam’s guidance.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hanan Bin Sudeyr, from Yazeed Bin Khalifa , and he is a man from the Clan of Al Haris Bin Ka’ab who said,

‘I heard him saying, ‘I went to Al-Medina and Ziyad Bin Ubeyd Al-Harisy was over it (the governor). So I sought permission to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, and I went over to him<sup>asws</sup>, and greeted him<sup>asws</sup>, and managed to sit in my (normal) place. So I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘I am a man from the Clan of Al-Haris Bin Ka’ab, and Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic has Guided me to your<sup>asws</sup> love and cordiality for you<sup>asws</sup>, the People<sup>asws</sup> of the Household’. So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘And how have you been Guided to our<sup>asws</sup> cordiality, the People<sup>asws</sup> of the Household, for by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, our<sup>asws</sup> love in the Clan of Al-Haris Bin Ka’ab, is scarce’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘So I said to himasws, ‘May I be sacrificed for youasws! There is a slave of mine, from Khurasan, and he is a bleacher and for him are four fellow countrymen, and they tend to invite each other every Friday. So the invitation occurs upon a man from them, and the turn comes to my slave every five Fridays. So he makes Al-Nabeez for them, and the meat. He said that when they are free from the meal and the meat, he comes with a bowl and fills it with Al-Nabeez. Then he comes with a clean jug. So when a person from them takes it, it is said to him, ‘Do not drink it until you send Blessings upon Muhammadsaww and the Progenyasws of Muhammadsaww (Salawaat)’. Thus I was guided towards yourasws loved by this slave’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘So he<sup>saww</sup> said to me: ‘Iasws advise you to be good with him and convey the greetings from me<sup>asws</sup>, and say to him that Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> Bin Muhammad<sup>asws</sup> is saying to you: ‘Consider this drink which you are drinking, for if a lot of it were to intoxicate, so do not go near the little of it, for Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Every intoxicant is prohibited’, and said: ‘Whatever a lot of it intoxicates, so a little of it is prohibited’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘So I went to Al-Kufa and I conveyed the slave, the greetings from Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> Bin Muhammad<sup>asws</sup>. So he wept, then said to me, ‘Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> Bin Muhammad<sup>asws</sup> attached such importance to me to the extent that he<sup>asws</sup> conveyed the greetings to me?’ I said, ‘Yes, and he<sup>asws</sup> has told to me to tell you: ‘Consider this drink of yours which you are drinking it, for if it was such that a lot of it were to intoxicate, so do not go near a little of it, for Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Every intoxicant is Prohibited, and whatever a lot of it intoxicates, so a little of it is prohibited’, and he<sup>asws</sup> advised me regarding you. Therefore go, for you are free for the Face of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the High’. So the slave said, ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! It is a drink which will not enter inside me for as long as I remain in the world’.
en.sarwar: 16. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il and Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hanan ibn Sadir from Yazid ibn Khalifah and he is a man from banu al-Harith ibn Ka‘b who has said the following:

“I once went to al-Madinah when Ziyad ibn ‘Ubayd Allah al-Harithiy was the governor. I asked permission to visit abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam. I then visited and offered him (the Imam) the greeting of peace and took my place. I then said to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘I am from banu al-Harith ibn Ka‘b and Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has granted me guidance to your love and affection toward Ah/ al-Bayt. He (the narrator) has said that abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, then asked, ‘How were you guided to love of Ahl al- Bayt? By Allah our love in banu al-Harith ibn Ka‘b is very little.’

He (the narrator) has said that I then said, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, I have a Khurasaniy slave. He works as bleacher and he has four fellows from his town. They invite each other every Friday to the place of one of them. In every five Fridays, my slave has one day and he prepares al-Nabidh and meat for them. When they finish food and meat he brings a bowl and fills it with al-Nabidh, then brings a jug, when one of them wants to drink he is told not to drink until he says, ‘O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause.’ I received guidance to loving you because of this slave.

He (the narrator) has said that he (the Imam) said to me, ‘Give him good advice, convey my greeting of peace to him and say to him, ‘Ja‘far ibn Muhammad says to you, “You must look into the drink that you drink. If a large quantity of it is intoxicating liquor then do not go close to its small quantity also; the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘All intoxicating liquor is unlawful.’ He (the Messenger of Allah) said, ‘Whatever is intoxicating liquor in large quantity, it in a small quantity is also unlawful.””

He (the narrator) has said that I went to al-Kufah and conveyed the greeting of peace to him from Ja‘far ibn Muhammad, ‘Alayhi al-Salam. He wept and asked me, ‘Did Ja‘far ibn Muhammad pay this much attention to me? He (the Imam) offered to me the greeting of peace! ’ I then said, ‘Yes, he (the Imam) did and he (the Imam) instructed me to inform you that you must look to the drink which you drink. If it is intoxicating liquor in large quantity, then do not go near to its small quantity; the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, “All intoxicating liquor is unlawful and whatever is intoxicating liquor in large quantity is unlawful in small quantity also.” He (the Imam) has recommended me to be good to you. Therefore, I set you free. You can go free for the sake of Allah, most High.’ The slave then said, ‘It is the kind of drink that will never go in my belly as long as I live in this world.’”
